card_surface: Linear's card face uses an extremely compressed VCS treatment that aligns with its minimal aesthetic. By default, an issue card in the board view shows a small Git branch-fork glyph (a single icon) when one or more linked PRs/branches exist; the glyph's colour and form encode state — open (grey/neutral), in review (variant), merged (filled/coloured), and closed-without-merge (muted). When multiple PRs are linked the icon can carry a numeric count (e.g. branch-icon + '2'). The 'Pull Requests and Commits' display option in View Options toggles this property on or off in both board and list layouts; teams that hide it see no PR signal on the card face at all. Branch name, PR title and CI check details do NOT render on the card face — they live in the side panel. There is no separate CI badge on the card; CI state is only inferred indirectly through the PR icon and the issue's workflow status (e.g. 'Ready to Merge'). This is the most-cited 'parity benchmark' for minimal card-surface design: one icon, one colour, one optional count.
detail_panel: Linear's issue detail view (right-side slide-in panel or full-page view) renders a structured PR/Git widget below the description. Each linked PR is its own row showing: repository name, PR number (e.g. #1234), PR title, branch name (head -> base), author avatar, current PR state pill (Draft / Open / In Review / Merged / Closed), and a relative timestamp. Display options allow showing/hiding additional fields including repository, failed checks, and preview links. Reviewer state appears as part of the PR row (reviewer avatars and 'review requested' indicator); approvals sync from GitHub. A dedicated Reviews sidebar section (separate from the per-issue panel) lists all PRs awaiting the user's review and PRs they authored, grouped into Todo / You're reviewing / Completed buckets, with bi-directional comment sync. Commit list and branch activity also appear inline in the issue's activity feed. The newer Releases feature adds a sidebar property showing which release(s)/environment(s) the issue has reached. Test runs are not native — they appear via third-party integrations (Testmo, Qase, Testiny, Testsigma, TestLodge, Tuskr, Browserstack) as linked attachments rather than a first-class Tests tab.
state_coupling: Linear's state coupling is the canonical reference implementation for PR-driven workflow automation, and it is configurable per-team-workflow rather than per-repo. The default automation is: branch created or PR opened -> issue moves to 'In Progress'; PR marked Ready for Review (or review requested) -> issue moves to a configured 'In Review' state; PR merged -> issue moves to 'Done' (Completed). Teams can override each trigger and the target status in Workflow settings on a per-team basis. Additional automation: issues can move to a 'Ready to Merge' state when the PR has passed all required checks (available for both GitHub and GitLab). If an issue has multiple open PRs, Linear waits for all of them to be merged before triggering the merge automation. Granularity is per-team-workflow (not per-repo or per-branch); the same team's automation applies to all linked repos. Coupling is opt-in at the team level but ships with sensible defaults so most teams keep it on. Auto-close behaviour on merge (Done vs. just status update) is also configurable. Draft PRs do not trigger the 'In Review' transition — only ready PRs do.
draft_vs_ready_state: Linear treats GitHub Draft PRs as a distinct first-class state. When a draft PR linked to an issue is opened, the PR shows up labelled 'Draft' inside the Linear issue's PR row; the issue stays in 'In Progress' rather than moving to 'In Review'. When the PR is marked Ready for Review on GitHub, Linear's automation fires and moves the issue to the configured 'In Review' status. On the card face the visual distinction is subtle — the same branch-fork glyph is used, but its colour/form reflects the underlying status (draft typically rendered in a neutral/muted tone, ready/in-review in a more prominent tone). Display options allow users to choose whether draft PRs are shown at all on cards, so teams can hide them and only surface ready PRs. The draft state is also visible in the Reviews sidebar.
review_state: Review state is surfaced primarily in the detail panel and in the dedicated Reviews sidebar, not on the card face. On the issue panel, the PR row shows reviewer avatars and a 'review requested' indicator; once approvals come in from GitHub they appear alongside the PR. The Reviews sidebar (currently in alpha, GA rolling out) lists PRs grouped as Todo / You're reviewing / Completed with bi-directional comment sync to GitHub. When a review is requested on a linked PR, Linear can automatically move the issue to a configured 'In Review' workflow state — surfacing the blocker via state change rather than a separate badge. Approval counts (e.g. '2/2 approved') and blocking-review indicators are not rendered on the card face; they live inside the PR row in the panel and in the Reviews sidebar. Notifications for review feedback, build failures, and approval requests flow into the Linear Inbox.
dod_checklist: Linear has no first-class Definition of Done checklist field. Teams implement DoD through one of three patterns: (1) inline markdown task lists in the issue description (lightweight, not roll-up reportable); (2) sub-issues, which Linear treats as separate first-class issues with their own statuses, assignees, and estimates — a parent issue shows a sub-issue progress count and a small progress ring/bar based on completed sub-issues; or (3) Issue Templates / Form Templates, which can pre-populate a description with a standard DoD checklist for a given issue type. Linear offers a keyboard shortcut (Cmd+Shift+O) to convert a markdown checklist into sub-issues. Completion percentage is shown at the parent level via sub-issue rollup and at the project/milestone level (milestone shows % of issues completed). DoD does NOT gate state transitions — there is no native rule preventing a story from being marked Done if its checklist is incomplete. Card-face treatment: sub-issue count appears as a small 'N/M' indicator on the parent card; checklist completion in the description is not surfaced on the card.
test_linkage: Linear has no native test management. Test linkage is provided entirely through third-party integrations, which surface as linked attachments and side-panel rows rather than a structured Tests tab. Supported integrations include Testmo, Qase, Testiny, Testsigma (Test Management by Testsigma), TestLodge, Testomat, Tuskr, and Browserstack Test Management. Typical flow: when a test fails in the test management tool, an issue is created or updated in Linear with the failure details; passing tests can sync back as comments or attachments. None of these surface a coverage badge or pass/fail count on the card face. CI test results (from GitHub Actions, CircleCI etc.) are treated as PR check status — collapsed into the PR row in the detail panel and into the 'Ready to Merge' workflow automation. CI pass/fail is therefore a separate axis from test-management linkage in Linear's data model.
cicd_status: CI/CD status is partially surfaced but never as a first-class card-face badge. In the detail panel's PR row, failed checks can be shown (toggle in display options); individual check names from GitHub Actions and other CI providers sync through. The primary way Linear represents CI status is via the 'Ready to Merge' workflow automation — when all required checks pass on a linked PR, the issue can auto-advance to a configured 'Ready to Merge' state. Supported providers: any CI integrated with GitHub or GitLab Checks (GitHub Actions, CircleCI, Buildkite, etc.), plus the newer Releases CI/CD integration which pulls deployment events. CI pass/fail is NOT rendered as its own icon on the card face — it is communicated indirectly through PR icon colour, issue workflow status, and the Inbox (build failure notifications). A failing CI check on a linked PR does not auto-flag the story as a risk; teams rely on the Inbox notification and the configured workflow state.
release_tagging: Linear's release model is the Releases feature (rolled out 2026-04-30 to Business and Enterprise plans). The data model is structured: a Release Pipeline (one per product/environment combination), containing Releases. Each release has a name, a commit SHA, an environment, and a set of associated issues. Pipelines can be Continuous (specialised UI for constant flow) or Scheduled (with stages and release dates). Issues are auto-grouped into releases by scanning new commits for Linear issue references (e.g. ENG-123). An issue can belong to multiple releases (different environments / pipelines). On the issue list view, release badges appear inline (e.g. 'iOS, nightly, internal'); the properties sidebar shows release info alongside other issue properties; users can filter by release, stage, or pipeline. The detail panel sidebar shows scheduled releases and their contained issues. Older or non-Releases workflows still use Cycles (sprint-like time buckets) and Projects as containers, but neither is a true release-tag. Business plan allows up to 15 pipelines; Enterprise is unlimited.
aggregation: Aggregation in Linear is partial. Parent issues with sub-issues show a sub-issue progress count (e.g. '3/5' completed) on the parent card and a small progress ring, but this is based on issue status — not on PR/branch/CI state. There is no native 'X of N stories have merged PRs' rollup on the Feature/Epic equivalent (Project or parent issue) card face. Projects show: overall completion %, a project graph (auto-generated once issue data is collected, updated hourly with 7-day granularity), and per-milestone completion %. Releases aggregate at the release level — a release shows the set of issues included and their statuses, effectively rolling up 'what shipped' but not 'how many had merged PRs'. The branch-icon glyph on a parent card does not roll up child PR state. This is consistently identified as a gap across tools, and Linear is no exception — the rollup is workflow-state based, not VCS-state based.
environment_deployment_target: Environment / deployment target is now first-class in Linear via the Releases feature (April 2026). Releases integrates with CI/CD tools (GitHub Actions, CircleCI, Buildkite, custom webhooks) to track which environment (dev, staging, UAT, production) and which version (commit SHA) each issue has reached. Issue statuses auto-update when associated code lands in production — so 'Done' can mean 'live to customers' rather than just 'merged'. Visual treatment: release/environment badges appear inline in list view rows (e.g. 'iOS, nightly, internal'); the properties sidebar carries release metadata; multiple environments can be shown simultaneously when an issue is included in multiple pipeline releases. Pipelines are configured per product/environment combination, so the same issue can be tracked through staging then production as separate releases. Deployment events attach via webhook from the CI/CD system. This is positioned as a deployment-context layer rather than a single environment badge — teams can see the full progression (e.g. internal -> nightly -> bi-weekly -> production) per issue.
traceability_completeness: Linear does not surface a composite traceability indicator. There is no single visual element on the card (or in the panel) that reports 'this story has code + tests + DoD + deploy'. Each axis is tracked independently: PR state via the branch-fork icon and PR row; test linkage via third-party integration attachments; DoD via sub-issues or markdown checklists; deployment via Releases. Linear's design philosophy explicitly favours separate, simple signals over a composite badge — completeness is implied by the issue reaching a 'Done' state (which, with full automation enabled, requires PR merged AND CI passed AND release deployed). Traceability is therefore encoded into the workflow status itself rather than into a separate roll-up indicator. Incomplete traceability does not gate state transitions natively, though teams can build gating via the 'Ready to Merge' automation step or sub-issue completion rules.
design_pattern: Linear's design vocabulary is the most disciplined in the category and the most-cited parity benchmark for minimal VCS-on-card treatment. On the card face: a single small Git branch-fork glyph, with colour/form encoding state, and an optional count when multiple PRs are linked. The pattern is consistent across all issue types (story, bug, task) since Linear has a unified issue model with type as a property rather than a separate card layout. Empty state: when no PRs/commits are linked, the icon simply is not rendered — there is no placeholder, no greyed-out slot, no 'no branch' label. In the detail panel, the pattern shifts to a structured PR widget — one row per PR with repository / number / title / branch / state pill / author / reviewers, plus inline activity feed entries for commits. State is encoded in both colour AND a text pill in the panel (Draft / Open / In Review / Merged / Closed) — the card-face icon is the compressed version of the same vocabulary. Display Options let users toggle the property on/off, treating PR/commit indicators as opt-in noise reduction rather than always-on chrome. The pattern aligns with Sand's restrained philosophy: single icon + colour for compression, structured rows in the panel for depth. This is the model most prototypes (Shortcut, Height, Plane) imitate.
